headline: Trust is the foundation of effective teams—without it, collaboration becomes expensive and slow
universal_truth: Trust is built in drops and lost in buckets; consistency over time creates reliability
fun_facts: High-trust teams outperform low-trust teams by up to 50% in studies
Trust activates oxytocin in the brain, which reduces stress and increases cooperation
It takes approximately 66 days of consistent behavior to form a habit of trust
discussion_questions: How do you know when you trust someone?
How do you rebuild trust after it's broken?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Watch a team that trusts each other—they move fast, communicate effortlessly, take risks. Watch a team without trust—every decision requires checking, verifying, protecting. Trust is invisible infrastructure. Without it, everything slows down.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Trust seems like a feeling, but it's actually a prediction—a bet that someone will behave as expected. What creates this willingness to depend on others?

options.text: Trust builds through consistency over time—people doing what they said they'd do, repeatedly, until reliability is proven
options.response: Yes. Trust isn't given—it's earned through evidence. Each kept promise, each reliable action, adds to the trust account. Consistency is the currency.

options.text: Trust comes from liking someone and having good intentions
options.response: Good intentions help, but trust requires proof through actions...

q1.title: Trust as Efficiency
q1.script: Low-trust environments require contracts, oversight, verification—all expensive. High-trust environments move faster with less friction. Trust isn't just nice; it's economically essential. Organizations with high trust outperform by wide margins.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Trust as Efficiency"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Vulnerability First
q2.script: Research shows trust often starts with vulnerability—someone takes a risk first. Leaders who admit mistakes create trust faster than those who seem perfect. Showing trust can generate trust.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Asymmetric Building
q3.script: Trust builds slowly and breaks quickly—built in drops, lost in buckets. One betrayal can destroy years of consistent behavior. This asymmetry means protecting trust is more important than building it.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Trust is built in drops and lost in buckets. Consistency over time creates reliability. Protect trust like the precious asset it is.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 202. Tomorrow, we'll explore when people disagree—handling conflict. Until then, be consistent in one area where you want to build trust.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Trust Deposit - Be Consistent
growTrack.activity: Identify one relationship where you want more trust. What consistent action could you take daily or weekly to build it? Trust is an account—make small deposits regularly. One kept promise at a time.
